claim: Operation Vigilant Sentry is the Department of Homeland Security's standing operation for intercepting maritime migration in the Caribbean and the Florida Straits. It was "first approved in 2004," run by the Homeland Security Task Force–Southeast (established 2003) — the Coast Guard, DHS, and state and local partners — and since August 2022 has surged assets against the highest maritime-migration levels the Coast Guard had seen in three decades. In 2024 the Florida Department of Law Enforcement spent $765,000 to equip the operation with Cognyte's FalcoNet cell-site simulators — the Israeli phone-tracking system also mounted in the $4.5 million surveillance vans Texas bought in 2026. (The device the Forbes reporting on Texas describes as recently authorized is, at the operational level, a two-decade-old DHS program.)
